summary.headline: Aequs H1 FY27 revenue rose 50% YoY to INR8,046m, but consumer EBITDA breakeven (Q4 FY27) was deferred and consumer segment EBITDA loss widened to INR401m in Q2.
summary.overview: H1 FY27 consolidated revenue grew 50% YoY to INR8,046m, led by aerospace (up 42% in H1) with Q2 revenue at INR4,091m (up 45% YoY). Consolidated reported EBITDA fell to INR245m in Q2 (6% margin vs 16% a year ago), driven by consumer ramp costs now being expensed after commercial operations began. Management deferred the consumer EBITDA breakeven target, previously Q4 FY27, and is recalibrating the consumer plan, while aerospace is described as on track. A INR6,500m promoter preferential warrant issue and a planned INR800m term loan were announced to fund capex.

segments.name: Aerospace
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR3,514m (+44% YoY, +9% QoQ) at ~22% segment EBITDA margin (INR783m, +24% YoY); H1 revenue +42% and segment EBITDA +29%. Aerospace contributed 86% of Q2 revenue and 84% of H1 revenue.

segments.name: Consumer (toys and consumer electronics)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR577m (+52% YoY) and H1 revenue INR1,311m vs INR632m last year. Segment EBITDA loss INR401m in Q2 and INR763m in H1; management attributes the loss to new capacity costs now expensed plus new-variant and headcount costs.

segments.name: Joint ventures (proportionate)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR4,480m (+44% YoY) with EBITDA INR331m (7% margin); H1 revenue INR8,781m (+48%) with EBITDA INR638m (7% margin), JV EBITDA +47% YoY in H1.

guidance_outlook: Consumer EBITDA breakeven, previously guided for Q4 FY27, is being recalibrated; no new date given while management evaluates scenarios.
Aerospace described as on track for the year; management says 'we're on target' on aerospace revenue and EBITDA for FY27 without numbers.
Overall 4-6x growth guidance by 2031 is reiterated.
Consumer PAT-positive guidance is FY30; consumer EBITDA breakeven utilisation is about 50%, and utilisation target by year-end remains 40-50%.
FY27 capex was initially guided at INR660 crore; management says it may come in much lower, with H1 capex of about INR160 crore and H2 expected to be similar, skewed to aerospace.
Working capital target of about 120 days is reiterated; inventory unwinding expected around Q1 FY28.
Toy business: Mattel expected to be the predominant customer by Q4 FY27 as the legacy customer phases out.
capex_capacity: Aerospace: 238 parts added in Q2 (+4% QoQ), taking the portfolio to 5,978 products; 9 CNC machines added, taking the fleet to 229, with 2.12 million annualised machining hours.
Aerospace utilisation 69% in Q2 (+8% YoY), 76% in India, despite added capacity.
Hosur (250-acre SEZ and DTA site): groundbreaking done; first-phase investment starts Q4 FY27; commercial production expected FY29, covering aero engine and landing gear components with a JV partner.
Consumer: most capacity is already in place; investment will be paced to customer schedules, with a larger share of capex going to aerospace.

Proposed INR650 crore funding allocation: about INR289 crore capex, about INR100 crore working capital, about INR100 crore for JV and strategic investments, the balance for general corporate purposes; about INR800 crore of term loans planned alongside.
demand_pricing: Aerospace order book reached USD 1.1 billion, up 9% in the quarter; typical execution cycle is 5-7 years, with some contracts up to 15 years.

Post-quarter, a new long-term agreement was signed with, and the relationship expanded to, 6 Safran entities, including a landing gear contract for Hosur; some of these qualifications are new capabilities expected to commercialise from FY29.
Management says aerospace has no pricing pressure under long-term contracts, and materials are passed through to customers.
Titanium content is rising in aerospace, which lifts material cost and weighs on segment margin in the short term.

Consumer ramp slower than expected: customer qualifications took longer, supply chain component shortages affected toy output, and weather disrupted logistics. Management says customer demand has not weakened.
Customer relationship: Mattel is the new key toy customer; the legacy toy customer is phasing out.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revised FY27 guidance for consumer and aerospace revenue and EBITDA, and what are the ATP ramp and failure rates?
qa_highlights.answer: Aerospace is 'pretty much on track'; consumer is being recalibrated and management will return with a year-end landing point. No ATP failure-rate data was given.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY28 external equity raise still on track after the promoter infusion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says capital is still needed to reach the 4-6x growth target by 2031, and a potential FY28 capital raise remains under consideration.

qa_highlights.question: What are the consumer scenarios, year-end utilisation target and capex spent to date?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation target remains 40-50%. H1 capex was about INR160 crore, mainly aerospace; FY27 capex may come in well below the INR660 crore original guidance, with more going to aerospace and less to consumer.

qa_highlights.question: Why did aerospace EBITDA grow much slower than revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cites a lower share of other income versus last year, higher SG&A and programme-management investment, and higher titanium content. It calls this timing rather than a trend change.

qa_highlights.question: Will consumer utilisation or cost pressure from an OEM push the business past any milestone?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the customer is still working with the company on utilisation and sees no demand loss; the consumer EBITDA breakeven level is about 50% utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the consumer electronics bottleneck and when do inventories normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Shortfalls came from a product update that required requalification and in-house capability building, plus toy component shortages. Inventory should normalise around Q1 FY28, and working capital days are targeted around 120.

risks_watch: Consumer EBITDA breakeven has slipped from Q4 FY27 with no new date; consumer loss widened QoQ to INR401m as revenue fell to INR577m.
Net debt to equity rose to 0.5x from 0.2x at March end; borrowings up INR1,576m in H1, with a planned INR800m term loan.
Aerospace EBITDA margin compression (EBITDA growth well below revenue growth) and the need for further SG&A and programme-management spending.
Consumer ramp risk: qualification cycles, component shortages, and weather-related logistics disruption, with Mattel volume ramp due by Q4 FY27.
Promoter warrant balance of INR3,250m is due by end-December next year; the FY28 external equity raise is still under consideration.
Proposed amalgamation of three wholly owned subsidiaries was not approved under the fast-track route; next steps are under evaluation.
summary.management_tone: Confident on aerospace and its long-term order book, but cautious and at times evasive on consumer: management declined to give a new breakeven date, revised consumer scenarios, or revenue breakeven levels, saying it would return with more detail.
key_quotes: In consumer, our customer programs continue to progress, but Q2 volumes ramp was slower than what we had anticipated.
We see this as a shift in the timing, not a change in the underlying opportunity.
Our order book reached USD 1.1 billion, up 9% this quarter, alongside further expansion of our portfolio.
What has changed is the pace. We remain confident in the trajectory, and we'll keep you updated on our progress.
